name: Question 2
worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=5{x}^{2}+7\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=10x \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡x\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x=-\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula for integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (5{x}^{2}+7)\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(5{x}^{2}+7)(-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)-\int (-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)(10x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-(5{x}^{2}+7)\operatorname{cos}⁡x+10\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Again, we use integration by parts to evaluate $\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x & \,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡x & \,⟹\,v=\int \operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\int \operatorname{sin}⁡x\,dx \\  & =x\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant. 

So, we get that the indefinite integral is

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (5{x}^{2}+7)\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =-(5{x}^{2}+7)\operatorname{cos}⁡x+10\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =-(5{x}^{2}+7)\operatorname{cos}⁡x+10(x\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x+D) \\  & =-(5{x}^{2}+7)\operatorname{cos}⁡x+10x\operatorname{sin}⁡x+10\operatorname{cos}⁡x+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=10D.$

Finally, we can work out the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }(5{x}^{2}+7)\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x & ={[-(5{x}^{2}+7)\operatorname{cos}⁡x+10x\operatorname{sin}⁡x+10\operatorname{cos}⁡x]}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =(-(5{\pi }^{2}+7)\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi +10\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡\pi +10\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi )-(-7\operatorname{cos}⁡0+10(0)\operatorname{sin}⁡0+10\operatorname{cos}⁡0) \\  & =(5{\pi }^{2}+7-10)-(-7+10) \\  & =5{\pi }^{2}-3-3 \\  & =5{\pi }^{2}-6\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2
?
Evaluate the following integral. Do not round the answer.
∫0π(5x2+7)sin⁡xdx=
5π2−6
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define u=5x2+7⟹dudx=10xdvdx=sin⁡x⟹v=∫dvdxdx=∫sin⁡xdx=−cos⁡x.

Using the formula for integration by parts, we get ∫(5x2+7)sin⁡xdx=∫udvdxdx=uv−∫vdudxdx=(5x2+7)(−cos⁡x)−∫(−cos⁡x)(10x)dx=−(5x2+7)cos⁡x+10∫xcos⁡xdx.

Again, we use integration by parts to evaluate ∫xcos⁡xdx. We take u=x⟹dudx=1,dvdx=cos⁡x⟹v=∫cos⁡xdx=sin⁡x.

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives ∫xcos⁡xdx=∫udvdxdx=uv−∫vdudxdx=xsin⁡x−∫sin⁡xdx=xsin⁡x+cos⁡x+D, where D is an integral constant.

So, we get that the indefinite integral is ∫(5x2+7)sin⁡xdx=−(5x2+7)cos⁡x+10∫xcos⁡xdx=−(5x2+7)cos⁡x+10(xsin⁡x+cos⁡x+D)=−(5x2+7)cos⁡x+10xsin⁡x+10cos⁡x+C, where C=10D.

Finally, we can work out the definite integral: ∫0π(5x2+7)sin⁡xdx=[−(5x2+7)cos⁡x+10xsin⁡x+10cos⁡x]0π=(−(5π2+7)cos⁡π+10πsin⁡π+10cos⁡π)−(−7cos⁡0+10(0)sin⁡0+10cos⁡0)=(5π2+7−10)−(−7+10)=5π2−3−3=5π2−6
